summary.headline: Stove Kraft Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41.3% YoY to INR480.6 crore, with EBITDA up 50.9% to INR53.8 crore and margin at 11.2%.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the strongest first quarter since inception, with revenue of INR480.6 crore (up 41.3%), gross profit of INR190.4 crore (up 46%) and PAT of INR17.1 crore (up 63.5%). Induction Cooktops grew 315.9% YoY and were about 27% of revenue, while small appliances and gas cooktops moderated because capacity and people were diverted to induction. Price hikes in domestic and export markets were used to pass on input cost inflation, supporting gross margin expansion of 127 bps. Working capital rose to 45 days on festive inventory build-up, and management guided to Q2 growth despite a high base.

financial_highlights.change: Higher than Q4 FY26; better than Q1 FY26 (69 days)

segments.name: Induction Cooktops (ICT)
segments.commentary: Grew 315.9% YoY and contributed 27% of revenue (about INR130 crore per analyst calculation). Management expects ICT to reach at least 20% of revenue for the year and about 2x last year on an annualised basis.

segments.name: Pressure Cookers
segments.commentary: Grew 41.3% YoY; management says it is the largest by volume at current run rate, with capacity additions under way.

segments.name: Non-stick cookware
segments.commentary: Grew 21.8% YoY and contributed 21% of revenue.

segments.name: Small appliances and gas cooktops
segments.commentary: Moderated temporarily due to capacity diversion to induction; small appliances still make up 27.5% of revenue mix. Management says capacity has since been augmented.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce 31.8% of revenue, general trade 28.6% (up 56.2% YoY, strongest in three years), exports 15.3%, modern retail 13%, and retail 8.7% (up 86.3% YoY). Added 17 franchise stores in the quarter, targeting 500 Pigeon exclusive outlets by end-2027.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 revenue expected to grow YoY over Q2 FY26 (about INR475-480 crore base), though not necessarily at Q1's growth rate.
Gross margin expected to improve at least 1% YoY; management views 40-42% as the sustainable gross margin band.
EBITDA margin targeted to rise at least 1 pp YoY, reaching 14-15% within two to three years.
Long-term PAT margin trajectory of 7-8% over two to three years, per management comments on a TV interview.
Non-induction categories targeted to grow about 15%+ consistently, with a stated aim near 20%; overall growth targeted at 15-20%.
Exports plus IKEA expected to reach about 15% of revenue in the current and next year; IKEA full-scale could be 5-6% of business. IKEA supplies to start in Q2 FY27.
Retail: profitable above INR2.5 lakh sales per store per month; currently about INR4.3 lakh, target at least INR5 lakh.
Triply cookware circle production in China JV expected by December 2026; automated pressure cooker line ready by end Q3.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing facilities set up in the last few quarters are all up and running, per management.
Pressure cooker capacity being added to meet unmet demand; a fully automated pressure cooker line is being set up, ready by end of Q3 FY27.
Small appliance capacity was diverted to induction and infrared products in Q1; management says it has since been augmented.
Triply cookware: JV with a Chinese partner, reportedly among the largest facilities in China; machines being installed; commercial production expected by December 2026.
Chimney range converted from AC to BLDC motors (all but one model); built-in hobs also being pushed.
Outsourced some manufacturing via job work in Q1 to meet demand; management expects this to normalise as in-house capacity comes up.
demand_pricing: Induction cooktop demand remains above pre-war levels; management expects traction to continue but not at the initial spike levels.
Cost-plus pricing model: domestic price increases taken and export buying prices revised upward to pass on input cost inflation.
Gross margin improvement attributed to price corrections and a favourable mix, including stainless steel pressure cookers outgrowing aluminium.
Q1 exchange-offer programme (mainly in EBOs and general trade) cited as a regular seasonal driver; GPOs up about 80% and general trade up about 50%.
Festive calendar spread across Q2 and Q3 (Onam in August, Dussehra in early October, Diwali in November).
South region about 50% of general trade contribution; North and West growing faster from a smaller base.
Working capital: inventory build-up for festive season; management plans straight-line production through the year to smooth working capital.

Other expenses rose to about 18% of sales, driven by job work (+1.2 pp), marketing (+1.2 pp; spend about 3.5-3.6% of sales), franchise commission (about 1% of sales; franchise mix 55-56% vs 43%), and CSR front-loading (about INR94 lakh, about 3% of PBT).
